title: The Hut in the Forest

full_text:
A poor woodcutter lived on the edge of a deep forest with his wife and three daughters. One day, the eldest daughter was sent into the woods carrying dinner to her father, but mistaking the trail of millet he had scattered, she wandered deep into the thickets until night fell.

She spotted a solitary light shining from an old thatched hut. Knocking at the door, she was greeted by an elderly grey-haired man sitting at a rustic table, while around him lay an old speckled hen, a red cock, and a spotted cow. The girl asked for food and shelter. The old man asked his animals if they agreed, and they clucked and mooed their consent. The girl ate heartily of the porridge, but offered not a crumb to the faithful creatures, nor did she bid them goodnight. When she went upstairs to sleep, the floor gave way, dropping her into a dark cellar.

The second daughter suffered the exact same fate on the following day, selfishly feeding only herself and ignoring the beasts.

On the third day, the youngest daughter ventured out. Arriving at the hut, she greeted the old man with gentle warmth, stroked the hen and the cock, and gave the spotted cow a generous handful of sweet hay. She shared her supper with all three beasts before tasting a single spoonful herself, and made sure their water trough was filled.

When she awoke next morning, the tiny hut had transformed into a dazzling royal palace of marble and gold! The old man was revealed to be an enchanted prince, transformed by a sorcerer until a maiden of pure compassion should appear who treated beasts with the same loving honor as kings. The cellar opened to release the older sisters, who were sent to learn humility, while the youngest married the prince and lived in boundless harmony.
moral: Kindness shown to the smallest and humblest creatures unlocks the door to genuine blessing.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Hut in the Forest"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
